- `rung-C.patch`: rung C's text as the planner measured it. `compiler/BuiltinPrimitiveRewriter.java` (new, 134 lines, item 35's probe class re-based with three changes: its switch, the refusal of a helper string that names no static method, and `namesHelpers`), two hooks in `compiler/Parser.java` (+5 −2), the switch in `Shell.specificRepository` (+2), a reading of the foreign Java types as the one library's in walk's world in `compiler/NamingCzar.java` (+45), beside the prelude's table, and three compiled tests in `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`. Applies to the base alone. Natives-shape's gap 1 patch from `4a46fb83a`, which the planner first applied in its place (+14 −11), rewrote the table every reading shares and failed `NamingCzarJUTest.testForeign` in the compiled tracks; the record's section 4 gives both runs.
- `rung-W.patch`: rung W's text as the planner measured it. `interpreter/glue/StaticNativeApp.java` (new, 208 lines), its hook in `interpreter/glue/NativeApp.java` (+8), the first family's 21 strings (19 of `ZZ32`'s in `Library/FortressLibrary.fss`, 2 of `Int`'s in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss`), and five walk tests in `ProjectFortress/tests/`. Applies to the base alone. The two together are the batch's text.
- `count.sh`: F-32's classes counted again on a built tree, with the natives probe's own scripts read from `4a46fb83a`; writes `classified.tsv` and `movable.tsv`. `classified-base.tsv` and `movable-base.tsv` are its output on the base build.
- `movable.py`: which bindings of classes A and B can name their helper as a bare string today, by the helper's Java signature read through the foreign-type table of walk's world; `count.sh` runs it.
- `family-edits.py`: moves a family of `movable.tsv` onto its helpers by exact text (`family-edits.py <tree> movable-base.tsv ZZ32,Int` wrote 23 strings; the batch's text then put `CHOOSE`'s and `Int`'s `asFloat`'s back, by hand, for the reasons in the record's section 4).
- `run-four.sh` and `four-imports-base.tsv`: the report-only check of the library components microGPT imports outside the distance: a copy of the distance stage whose component list is the one file `FOUR_TARGET` names, run once per target on the base build, and the errors it printed.

## How to run them again

From a worktree seeded from a base build at `e0ec620a9`, set up as the `fortress-repo` skill's `build-and-caches.md` says:

    git apply explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/rung-C.patch explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/rung-W.patch
    ant compileAll        # then the library order, before the compiled tests
    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/h ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelper*Walk.* ProjectFortress/tests/ZZ32DivisionByZeroWalk.fss
    ONE_JVM=1 explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-N/merged-tests/junit.sh c23 ProjectFortress/compiler_tests NativeHelperBindingCompiled.test XXXNativeHelperMisfitCompiled.test XXXNativeHelperMisspeltCompiled.test
    explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh tmp/distance.txt tmp/distance        # in the background
    explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh tmp/count.txt tmp/count         # in the background

and for the count, from any built tree: `explorations/compile-ladder/plan-23/probes/count.sh <tree> <out-dir>`.

#!/bin/bash
# run-four.sh: climb batch 23 planner copy of tools/distance/run.sh, its twelve components replaced by the one target that
# FOUR_TARGET names (FOUR_TARGET=Library/System.fss run-four.sh <out> <scratch>), for the report-only check of the library
# components microGPT imports outside the distance (reviews/batch-22-review.md, finding 3). Run from a built tree with
# FORTRESS_HOME set to it and a scratch folder outside it; one run per target, so that each is checked with every stage.
# The gate's distance stage: the compiled checker over the whole interpreter library, the
# twelve prelude apis and their twelve components, every stage of every unit run whatever
# the earlier stages reported, so that nothing hides behind an early return; one table.
#
# Why it exists: Pavol's answer 11 (POSITIONS.md, 2026-09-26): the full measurement of the
# distance to the switch-over "becomes a report-only stage of phase 3's gates, whose job is
# driving it down". The checker-count stage beside it (../checker-count/run.sh) sees only
# the errors before each api's early return, 62 of about 1,740 on 2026-09-27.
#
# Run from $FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh sourced, after ant compileAll:
#
#     explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/run.sh <out-file> [scratch-dir] [setting]
#
# It writes the table to <out-file> and prints it. Nothing in the tree is touched: the
# shadow sources and classes, the driver, the checker's caches (-Dfortress.caches) and the
# JVM's temporary directory (so Rats! leaves nothing in /tmp) go to the scratch directory
# (default: $TMPDIR or /tmp), and the caches are deleted at the end. It never removes
# /tmp/fortress*rats, which other runs on the machine use. Exit 0 if the table was
# produced, 1 if it could not be. One JVM, -Xmx4g, one busy core: 789 s on the idle 4-CPU
# container on 2026-09-27, 14 to 24 minutes under load 7 to 18 (switch-over-distance-flat.md
# section 5); the table's #seconds and #machine rows say what each run took and where.
#
# The setting: "any" by default, the compiled path with the implicit bound Any
# (DistanceMulti's -setting any: the extends-Object pre-desugaring off, as walk's, and the
# compiled-expression desugaring on, as the compile path's). Answer 11 names the compile
# path's setting; batch 7's question 1, answered (a) on 2026-09-27 (POSITIONS.md, the
# numerics plans), bounds an unbounded type parameter by Any, and under it the switch-over
# takes that bound for the compiled path (CLIMB-BATCH-7.md section 1, Q1), so the 372
# "bound Object" errors of the plain compile setting are the setting's, not the library's
# (switch-over-distance-flat.md sections 2.7 and 5: "under (a) the stage runs stage-any").
# On the tree of 2026-09-27 it differs from walk's setting by the compiled-expression
# desugaring's 12 abstract-method errors on bodyless functions, one export error and the
# variance checker's crash on Stream: 1,746 to 1,747 against 1,737 to 1,738 (FACTS.md,
# "The true distance to the switch-over"). The third argument, walk or compile, runs
# another setting, for a comparison with the measurements on file; the gate never passes it.
#
# The overloading checker's memo is off (-Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false), as in
# every run of the measurement: keyed on declaration pairs, it hides 27 to 35 errors
# depending on the build order (FACTS.md, "The overloading checker's memo hides errors
# by build order, so every count runs with it off ...").
#
# The sources beside this script are copies, taken 2026-09-27, so that the gate does not
# depend on a probe directory, as the checker-count stage's were: DistanceMulti.java from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance-flat/ (35ef70584); shadow-patch.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/desugar-codegen/ (e5d8cdbd2); add-patch.py and errors.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/ (a7e3df9ad, 14d2f9839); classify.py from
# perf-probes/prelude/distance-triage/ (e17a9badc); all unchanged but classify.py, which since
# row 577 finds the library places that name three of its classes by their declarations in
# the tree's sources ($FH, passed to table.py), not by line ranges. table.py is new: it
# counts as those scripts count and prints the rows below. The shadow classes are not
# copies: they are made from the tracked sources at every run by text edits that must each
# match exactly once (shadow-patch.py, add-patch.py), so there is no copied checker to go
# stale silently; an edit that no longer matches stops the run before the checker starts,
# and the table then says so in its #shadow row, with no counts.
#
# The table, tab-separated, every row tagged:
#   #distance   the setting, the switches and the twelve targets
#   #total      distinct errors; or "none:" and why, when no total was measured, as when a
#               target stopped with errors the stage does not count, such as a parse error
#   #kind       by kind (errors.py): exclusion, comprises, overloading, return-type, ...
#   #class      by root cause (classify.py, distance-triage.md section 2), with its name
#   #check      a disagreement: errors.py's and table.py's totals, or sites classify.py cannot
#               find in the tree's library source
#   #unit       by the unit that printed the error first
#   #crash      each declaration, stage or target the checker crashed on
#   #seconds    the run's wall time, and FortressLibrary's, the part that takes it
#   #machine    nproc, CPU model and MHz, load at start, JDK, FORTRESS_THREADS
#   #shadow     whether every shadow edit matched the tracked sources; the last row
# ../distance/compare.sh compares two tables. The run-to-run variation is 2 to 4 errors,
# in the comparisons' and Maybe's pairs and the joins of array bodies (switch-over-
# distance-flat.md section 5).
set -u

OUT=${1:-}
if [ -z "$OUT" ] ; then echo "usage: $0 <out-file> [scratch-dir] [any|walk|compile]" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
case "$OUT" in /*) ;; *) OUT="$PWD/$OUT" ;; esac
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:-$PWD}
D="$FH/explorations/coordinator/tools/distance"
SCRATCH=${2:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/distance.$$}
case "$SCRATCH" in /*) ;; *) SCRATCH="$PWD/$SCRATCH" ;; esac
SETTING=${3:-any}
case "$SETTING" in any|walk|compile) ;; *) echo "distance: unknown setting $SETTING" >&2 ; exit 1 ;; esac
FLAGS="-Dprobe.tolerant=true -Dprobe.all=true -Dfortress.analyzer.overload.cache=false"
COMPONENTS="${FOUR_TARGET:?}"

rm -rf "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp"
mkdir -p "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" "$SCRATCH/classes" "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" \
         "$(dirname "$OUT")" || exit 1
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed 's#:[^:]*/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache##')
if [ -z "$CP" ] ; then echo "distance: no classpath from bin/fortress_classpath" >&2 ; exit 1 ; fi
MACHINE="nproc=$(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | sed 's/^[^:]*: *//') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=${FORTRESS_THREADS:-unset}"

# 1. the shadows, from the tracked sources (perf-probes/prelude/switch-over-distance/make-shadows.sh's
#    steps), and the driver; a text edit that no longer matches is the one way this can go stale
SHADOW="every shadow edit matched the tracked sources"
if ! ( cd "$FH" && python3 "$D/shadow-patch.py" ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" \
                && python3 "$D/add-patch.py" "$SCRATCH/shadow-src" ) > "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: a shadow edit no longer matches the tracked sources: $(grep -E '^AssertionError' "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" | tail -1 | tr -s ' ' | cut -c1-200); see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -encoding UTF-8 -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/StaticChecker.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/TypeCheckPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/DesugarPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/phases/CodeGenerationPhase.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/Desugarer.java" \
        "$SCRATCH/shadow-src/com/sun/fortress/nodes_util/NodeComparator.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: the shadow sources no longer compile against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
elif ! javac -nowarn -cp "$CP" -d "$SCRATCH/classes" "$D/DistanceMulti.java" >> "$SCRATCH/shadows.txt" 2>&1 ; then
    SHADOW="STALE: DistanceMulti.java no longer compiles against the tree; see $SCRATCH/shadows.txt"
fi

# 2. the run: one JVM, the twelve components, FortressLibrary first so that its run checks
#    the twelve apis with every stage (DistanceMulti.java's header)
RC=
case "$SHADOW" in
  STALE*) : > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
  *) S=$(date +%s)
     ( cd "$FH" && timeout -k 30 5400 java -Xmx4g -Xss64m -XX:-OmitStackTraceInFastThrow \
           -Djava.io.tmpdir="$SCRATCH/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$SCRATCH/caches" $FLAGS \
           -cp "$SCRATCH/shadow-classes:$SCRATCH/classes:$CP" DistanceMulti -order check -setting "$SETTING" $COMPONENTS
     ) > "$SCRATCH/run.txt" 2>&1
     RC=$? ; ELAPSED=$(( $(date +%s) - S ))
     rm -rf "$SCRATCH/caches" "$SCRATCH/tmp" ;;
esac

# 3. the table. errors.py's tally and its one-row-per-error list stay in the scratch
#    directory for whoever needs the sites (compare-sites, the review); table.py's rows go
#    into the table, and their total is checked against errors.py's own count.
{
    printf '#distance\tsetting %s; %s; %s\n' "$SETTING" "$FLAGS" "$(echo $COMPONENTS | wc -w) components in one JVM (DistanceMulti -order check)"
    if grep -q '^### all seconds=' "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ; then
        python3 -B "$D/table.py" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" "$FH" > "$SCRATCH/rows.txt" 2>&1
        cat "$SCRATCH/rows.txt"
        python3 "$D/errors.py" "$SCRATCH/errors.tsv" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" > "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" 2>&1
        E=$(sed -n 's/^# \([0-9]*\) distinct errors.*/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/tally.txt")
        T=$(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "#total" { print $2 }' "$SCRATCH/rows.txt")
        case "$T" in none*) ;; *)
        [ "$E" = "$T" ] || printf '#check\terrors.py counts %s, table.py %s: the two normalisations differ on this run; see %s\n' "$E" "$T" "$SCRATCH/tally.txt" ;; esac
        printf '#seconds\t%s\tFortressLibrary %s\n' "${ELAPSED:-?}" "$(sed -n 's/^### done Library\/FortressLibrary.fss rc=-\{0,1\}[0-9]* seconds=\([0-9]*\)$/\1/p' "$SCRATCH/run.txt")"
    else
        case "$SHADOW" in
          STALE*) printf '#total\tnone: the checker did not run\n' ;;
          *) printf '#total\tnone: the run ended without its last line (rc=%s); see %s\n' "${RC:-?}" "$SCRATCH/run.txt" ;;
        esac
    fi
    printf '#machine\t%s\n' "$MACHINE"
    printf '#shadow\t%s\n' "$SHADOW"
} > "$OUT"

cat "$OUT"
echo "# distance: full output $SCRATCH/run.txt, rc=${RC:-not run}; errors.py's tally $SCRATCH/tally.txt"
grep -q '^#total	[0-9]' "$OUT"

coordinator/FACTS.md:170:- F-143 **Under walk, a type parameter whose bound mentions itself and that nothing at a call fixes is left open.** Such a bound is an F-bound, as in `mk[\T extends Cmp[\T\]\]()`. The open type, printed `OPEN`, is below every type, and every value matches it. A reduction or a comprehension that writes no static argument is first instantiated by its declared type or by its elements' join (F-228). So the open parameter reaches one only where neither fixes it: an empty `SUM` or `PROD` that no declared type directs, which takes `ZZ32`'s identity whatever its body's type (row 716), or a clause form whose declared type or join does not fit the bound (F-228). A call such as `mk()` also leaves it open. Where overloads are compared, a tuple, arrow or generic type that holds the open type admits no more than it would at `BottomType`: beside `pick(x: Any)`, `pick(x: (T,T))` does not take `(1, 2)`, though a lone `one(x: (T,T))` does (row 663, contested). In a probe by the rung's skeptic, the agent that checks a rung's work after its worker, a method declared over `T` in an object whose `T` stayed open was the most specific one, and so was chosen for every argument; no gated test holds this. A list comprehension written at such an open parameter, as `<|[\T\] x | x <- xs |>`, ends in `CastError` at its unwrap's cast, `cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\](cc)` (`Library/List.fss:179`), and so does `List`'s range subscript at a stride other than 1 on a list of that open element type, since the subscript writes `[\E\]` (row 825, contested). # The export check of FortressLibrary, run to its end

## In short

- **The 43 entries hide 115 differences, and 4 more.** The stock check names, of each trait, only the first member that differs, and stops at a trait whose api lists more members than its component. A shadow that compares every member, by name as well as by header, finds 115 differences that the stock rules report one trait at a time, in the 43 traits and objects. It also finds 4 more that the stock check accepts only because it matches a trait's members without their names. Section 2 lists them all.
- **Sorted (section 3):**

  | What clears it | Differences |
  |---|---|
  | 4h: `abstract` written in the api where the component's member has no body | 56 |
  | 4h: the api declares a bodyless member of the component that it lacks | 3 |
  | 4h: plain slips | 7 |
  | 4i: the check brought to `apis.tex` | 8 |
  | Neither, and no decision by my reading | 17 |
  | A decision | 6 |
  | Waits elsewhere: `Maybe`, `Just` and `Nothing` (P-90), `String` (P-155) | 5 + 13 |
  | **Total** | **115** |

  Two of 4h's 56, `QQ`'s `numerator` and `denominator`, also need a fix of the check: it compares their `self` types with the api's and the component's sides swapped (section 6, defect 3). The 4 differences that the stock check accepts by the name gap go 1 to neither, 2 to decisions and 1 to String.
- **The 4h patch: the distance goes from 5 to 28** (section 4). The export error stays, its entries 43 → 20. The two `BIG MIN` sites and the two OT sites stay. 23 new errors come, all `abstract-method`: 17 in `FortressBuiltin` (`BigNum` 15, `Int` 1, `Long` 1) and 6 in `RangeInternals` (the three open ranges, 2 each). Each one comes from an `abstract` line in `Integral` or `Range`, where the api of the trait that implements the member does not show the component's concrete member. With 19 more api lines that show those members, the 23 go and nothing else comes: the distance is 5 again, with 20 entries.
- **4i after 4h** clears 10 more differences (8, and String's 2): 51 → 41, entries 20 → 15. What then remains is the 25 differences of neither and of a decision, and the 16 of `Maybe` and `String` that are left after 4h and 4i.
- **Walk:** microGPT's quick pair passes on the patch, 7 of 7 each, and so do nine walk tests of the patched traits (section 4.4).
- **Found on the way** (section 6): the check matches members without their names. Its field comparison ignores names and modifiers, through a Scala newline. Its component-to-api half swaps its arguments into a one-sided self-type comparison. And the distance stage prints `#total 0` for a library that does not parse.

## 1. How it was measured

### The shadow

`export-check-shadow.patch` edits `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/ExportChecker.scala`, in a copy compiled into a scratch folder that comes ahead of the build on the class path. The stock check, which is the team's (`^5a68404fd`, the history's boundary), stops at two places:

- `equalListMembers` returns "missing members" when the api's trait lists more members than the component's (`ExportChecker.scala:768-769`), and else ends in `inAPI.forall(handleOne)` (`:787`).
- `allAbstractsMadePublic` ends in `inComp.forall` (`:749`).

The shadow makes both of them map over every member, and it keeps the stock verdict. Beside the verdict, it prints one `#XDIFF` line for each difference: the trait, the kind, the member, the api's and the component's spans, and the two headers. For every member it also looks up the members of the same name on the other side, which the stock check never does (section 6, defect 1).

Its kinds:

- **Header clauses:** `header-extends`, `header-excludes` and the rest.
- **The api's members:** `api-member-missing` (no member of the name in the component), `abstract-component-only`, `abstract-api-only`, `api-member-differs` (with the differing parts: static parameters, modifiers, parameter types, return type), and `api-matched-by-other-name` (the stock check accepts the member through a member of another name).
- **The component's abstract members:** `comp-abstract-absent`, `pair:abstract-component-only` (the other half of an api-side pair), `comp-abstract-differs` and `comp-abstract-matched-by-other-name`.

With `PROBE_EXPORT_4I` set in the environment, the shadow applies 4i (section 3.2).

=== 02d09a39f
The library's scalar extension generalised and its exclusion tower closed

Four sites in Library/FortressLibrary.fss, mirrored in .fsi:

- :4496-4504 (api :2540-2547), the block that was :4493-4517: the integer scalar-extension block
  `opr + - MIN MAX (Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\], ZZ32)` becomes eight generic
  declarations `[\T extends Number, I\]`, both operand orders, on the
  precedent of the `T extends Number` array operators at :2264-2279 and
  :2624-2637.
- :612 (api :409): `trait AnyIntegral extends { QQ } comprises { ZZ }`
  closes the numeric tower's one open comprises link; the api already
  closes `ZZ` at :536.
- :327-328 (api :250-251): the `AnyMultiplicativeRing` placeholder pattern
  of :338-339 (api :262-263) applied to `AdditiveGroup` -- a marker `trait
  AnyAdditiveGroup end` that `AdditiveGroup` extends.
- :2669 (api :1659): `Array3 excludes { Number, String, AnyAdditiveGroup,
  AnyMultiplicativeRing }`.

Why the tower has to be closed for the generic block to load beside
`AdditiveGroup.+` and `StandardTotalOrder.MAX`: the interpreter makes a
trait with a `comprises` clause exclude whatever every leaf of its
transitive comprises excludes (FType.java:281-297,
FTypeTrait.java:68-78). `ZZ32`'s leaves are the objects `Int` and
`IntLiteral`, which is why the shipped ground block loads; `RR64`'s leaves
included `AnyIntegral`, a trait with no comprises clause, which excludes
nothing, so nothing above `RR64` excluded the symbolic bound of a library
operator's type variable and the generic block over `T extends Number`
would be refused. With `AnyIntegral comprises { ZZ }` the tower is closed.
The marker trait and the `Array3` clause do the same for a user operator
whose non-self operand is an `Array3`.

The two tests, each run from an empty FORTRESS_CACHES, red on the tree
before this edit and green after:

- tests/ArrayScalarExtension.fss -- 24 checks of `+ - MIN MAX` in both
  operand orders over an `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, a `Matrix` and an
  `Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]`, the last pinning the shipped block's behaviour,
  which no test asserted. Before: "Failed to find any matching overload,
  args = (__DefaultVector[\RR64,3\],1.0)".
- tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss with the api fixture
  test_library/ArrayOperatorVocabulary.{fsi,fss} -- a user vocabulary over
  the standard arrays that must load beside the library's operators: two
  `MINMAX` over `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]`, the plane-wise `+` between a
  `Matrix` and an `Array3` in both orders, and two `juxtaposition`
  declarations at rank 3. Before: "... has a parameter with generic type,
  at least one pair of parameters must have excluding types" against
  `StandardTotalOrder.MINMAX`. One user declaration of an operator name is
  not checked against the library's (gap-ledger row 341), so the fixture
  declares two of each, as the programs that hit this do; the fixture goes
  in test_library/, the fourth entry on fortress.source.path, which is
  where this corpus keeps the apis its tests import.

Gate on this tree, caches wiped first: ant testSystem 384 tests (382 plus
these two), 0 failures; ant testFast 1,409 tests, 0 failures.

The five plain api defects of the interpreter library repaired

Eleven RangeInternals declarations take the Integral[\I\] bound the traits
they instantiate require, String's duplicated split pair is declared once,

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## The library's arrays and algebra

FACTS.md:206
- F-264 **In the interpreter's library, nine `Vector` and `Matrix` operators and three branches of the array factories get their declared type through the function `cast`, and so does the sub-array that `Array2`'s column and row subscripts pass to `Col` and `Row`.** `cast[\T\](x)` returns `x` if it has type `T`, and raises `CastError` if not (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:33-37`). The operators are `Vector`'s `+`, binary and unary `-`, `scale` and `pmul`, and `Matrix`'s `+`, binary and unary `-` and `scale`. Each builds its result with the inherited `map` or `ivmap`, typed `Array1` or `Array2`, and so through `replica`, the method that makes an array of the same layout. The factory branches are those of `__builtinFactory1`, `__immutableFactory1` and `__builtinFactory2` for an array whose lowest indices are 0, each cast to its factory's declared result type. The subscripts are `a[:, j]` and `a[i, :]`. Each builds its sub-array with a range subscript, which answers an unsized `Array`, and the cast gives it the sized `Array2` that the field of `Col` or `Row` takes. Five bodies build with `fill` or `tabulate` and need no cast, since `Vector` and `Matrix` redeclare those two at their own type (F-158): the factories `vector(v)`, `tabulatedVector` and `matrix(v)`, and `Matrix`'s `rmul` and `lmul`. So the compiled checker accepts all these bodies (the distance stage). Under walk each cast holds at the eight number types (`tests/VectorMatrixCastsWalk.fss`). A `Vector` whose `replica` answers an array that is not a `Vector`, or a `Matrix` whose `replica` answers one that is not a `Matrix`, raises `CastError` at the nine operators. When the casts landed, no walk value moved in the 42 test files that use the array family, compared value by value, or in four array demos; every test of the interpreter's suite passed, and so did microGPT's quick pair. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-array-sites/REPORT.md` sections 1 and 5 (each change with its sites; walk's runs); `compile-ladder/rung-array-sites/SKEPTIC.md` sections 2 (the four demos) and 3, finding 3 (the `CastError` case).

== explorations/coordinator/FACTS.md, ## The checker and the one library

FACTS.md:105
- F-250 **Inside a declaration, the compiled checker reads a `where` clause's trait constraint `X extends B` as a bound of `X`, and it adds a constraint on the declaration's own static parameter to that parameter's bound in the declaration's arrow (its function type), so a call is checked against it.** So a method's condition on its trait's or object's static parameter bounds that parameter in the method's body (`compiler_tests/WhereBoundMethodChecker`), and a call that breaks a function's own constraint is refused (`compiler_tests/XXXWhereBoundFunctionCall`, which refuses `g("s")`). A hole remains: a static argument written at a top-level call is not checked against that bound, so `g[\String\]("s")` is accepted (row 470). F-256 holds where the checker reads the constraints at a dotted call, at a type's use and at a `comprises` clause, with its other limits. The library edits that landed with this reading are F-242's (the generic `distribute`, and the `where` conditions on `SumReduction`'s `distribute` overloads for `MAX` and `MIN`) and F-85's (`additiveIdentity`'s and `multiplicativeIdentity`'s fallbacks written `cast[\T\](0)` and `cast[\T\](1)`, and `embiggen` typed `BigReduction[\T,T\]`). Detail: `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-distribute/REPORT.md` section 1.

(** The %#% and %:% operators serve as factories for parallel ranges. **)
opr #(lo:ZZ32, ex:ZZ32): CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]
opr #(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32), ex:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
opr #(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), ex:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

opr :(lo:ZZ32, hi:ZZ32): CompactFullRange[\ZZ32\]
opr :(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32), hi:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
opr :(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), hi:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange[\(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

(** Factories for incomplete ranges. **)
opr (x:ZZ32)# : LeftRange[\ZZ32\]
---

(** The # and : operators serve as factories for parallel ranges. **)
opr #(lo:ZZ32, ex:ZZ32): CompactFullParScalarRange = sized1Range(lo,ex)
opr #(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32), ex:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange2D =
    do (l1,l2)=lo; (x1,x2)=ex; sized2Range(l1,l2,x1,x2) end
opr #(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), ex:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange3D =
    do (l1,l2,l3)=lo; (x1,x2,x3)=ex
       sized3Range(l1,l2,l3,x1,x2,x3)
    end

opr :(lo:ZZ32, hi:ZZ32): CompactFullParScalarRange =
        bounded1Range(lo,hi)
opr :(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32), hi:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange2D =
    do (l1,l2)=lo; (h1,h2)=hi; bounded2Range(l1,l2,h1,h2) end
opr :(lo:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), hi:(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): CompactFullRange3D = do
    (l1,l2,l3)=lo; (h1,h2,h3)=hi
    bounded3Range(l1,l2,l3,h1,h2,h3)
  end

---
opr BIG ||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\]

opr BIG ||(g: Generator[\Any\]): String

(** This operator performs string concatenation, first converting
    its inputs (of type Any) to String if necessary, and separating
    non-empty components by a space. **)
opr BIG |||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\]

opr BIG |||(g: Generator[\Any\]): String

(** This operator performs string concatenation with newline
    separation, first converting its inputs (of type Any) to String if
    necessary. **)
opr BIG //(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,Maybe[\String\]\]
---
(** This operator performs string concatenation, first converting
    its inputs (of type Any) to String if necessary. **)
opr BIG ||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\] =
    Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\](
        identity[\String\],StringReduction,fn (x:Any)=> "" x)

opr BIG ||[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Any,String,String,String\](BIG ||(), g.map[\Any\](identity[\Any\]))

(** This operator performs string concatenation, first converting
    its inputs (of type Any) to String if necessary, and separating
    non-empty components by a space. **)
opr BIG |||(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\] =
    Comprehension[\Any,String,String,String\](
        identity[\String\],SpaceReduction,fn (x:Any)=> "" x)

opr BIG |||[\T\](g: Generator[\T\]): String =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\Any,String,String,String\](BIG |||(), g.map[\Any\](identity[\Any\]))

(** This operator performs string concatenation with newline
    separation, first converting its inputs (of type Any) to String if
    necessary. **)
opr BIG //(): Comprehension[\Any,String,String,Maybe[\String\]\] =

opr <|[\E\] xs: E... |>: List[\E\]
(** List comprehensions: *)
opr BIG <|[\T\]|>:Comprehension[\T,List[\T\],List[\T\],List[\T\]\]
opr BIG <|[\T\] g:Generator[\T\]|>:List[\T\]

(** Vararg factory for lists; provides aggregate list constants **)
opr <|[\E\] xs: E... |>: List[\E\] = list(xs)
opr BIG <|[\T\]|>: Comprehension[\T,List[\T\],AnyCovColl,AnyCovColl\] =
    covariantCompr[\T,List[\T\]\](fn (cc) => fromImmutableArray(cast[\CovariantCollection[\T\]\](cc).toImmutableArray()))
opr BIG <|[\T\] g:Generator[\T\]|>:List[\T\] =
    __bigOperatorSugar[\T,List[\T\],AnyCovColl,AnyCovColl\](BIG <|[\T\]|>(), g)

import io
p="tmp/r782/src/ExportChecker.scala"
t=io.open(p,encoding="utf-8").read()
old="""      val fnsInAPI  = api.functions
      val fnsInComp = component.functions
"""
new="""      val fnsInAPI  = api.functions
      val fnsInComp = component.functions
      if (System.getenv("AUDIT_782") != null) {
        // AUDIT row 782: every top-level operator of the api against the component's
        // declarations of the same operator, whatever key the relation files them under
        val compAll: List[FnDecl] = toSet(fnsInComp.firstSet).toList.flatMap(k =>
          toSet(fnsInComp.matchFirst(k)).toList.flatMap { case SDeclaredFunction(fd) => List(fd); case _ => Nil })
        for ( k <- toSet(fnsInAPI.firstSet) ; d <- toSet(fnsInAPI.matchFirst(k)) ) d match {
          case SDeclaredFunction(fd) if fd.getHeader.getName.isInstanceOf[Op] =>
            val same = compAll.filter(c => equalNames(c.getHeader.getName, fd.getHeader.getName))
            val ok = same.exists(c => equalFnHeaders(fd.getHeader, c.getHeader, false))
            val keyIn = fnsInComp.firstSet.contains(k)
            val verdict = if (ok) "MATCH" else if (same.isEmpty) "NONAME" else "DIFFER"
            val parts = same.map { c => (fd.getHeader, c.getHeader) match {
              case (SFnHeader(spL, mL, nL, _, thL, _, pL, rL), SFnHeader(spR, mR, nR, _, thR, _, pR, rR)) =>
                NodeUtil.getSpan(c).toString.replaceAll(".*/", "") + "{" + List("sparams" -> equalListStaticParams(spL, spR),
                  "mods" -> mL.equals(mR), "throws" -> equalOptListTypes(thL, thR),
                  "params" -> equalListParams(pL, pR), "ret" -> equalOptTypes(rL, rR)).filter(!_._2).map(_._1).mkString(",") + "}"
            }}
            System.out.println("@@Y782\\t" + verdict + "\\tkeyInComp=" + keyIn + "\\t" + fd.getHeader.getName + "\\t"
                               + NodeUtil.getSpan(fd).toString.replaceAll(".*/", "") + "\\t" + same.size + "\\t" + parts.mkString(" "))
          case _ =>
        }
      }
"""
assert t.count(old)==1
t=t.replace(old,new,1)
io.open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(t)
print("ok")
EOF

# Row 816's third way: the export check's reading (1), with the code generator closing the failure

## In short

- **Row 816's program dies even when `O` defines `f`.** The client's call is `invokeinterface P816Api$T.f()`. The interface `P816Api$T` is the component's class, and it declares only the members of the component's trait, so JVM resolution fails before the receiver's class `O` is looked at.
- **The smallest change is in the code generator.** The component's trait interface also declares, abstract, every method that the exported api's trait of the same name declares and the component's trait does not. That is about 30 lines in `CodeGen.java`, and the patch is at the end.
  - The new compiled test `ExportAbstractMemberCall` failed through the harness on the base and passed with the shadow.
  - `ant testQuick`: compiler 1317, library 86, othercompiler 263, with no failures (the base's gate had 1315 / 86 / 263; the two extra tests are the new test's link and run).
  - The shadow adds no method to any class of the compiler's prelude.
- **The change closes 5 of the 9 failing shapes I measured.** These are: a plain method, a getter, a generic trait, a body from a sub-trait, and a body from a second trait in the `extends` list.
- **It leaves 4 shapes failing:**
  - `AbstractMethodError` when no object defines the member (row 816's own program, which the checker accepts);
  - `AbstractMethodError` when the component's trait declares the member at another header;
  - `AbstractMethodError` when the object narrows the return type, because no bridge method is emitted;
  - `NoSuchMethodError` for a functional method, because no static wrapper is emitted.
- **Walk needs nothing.** It finds the method on the object by name.
- **The library's 12 members:**
  - Any program can call all 12 through the trait's type.
  - 3 of them (`ActualReduction`'s `empty` and `join`, `AnyMaybe`'s `holds`) already resolve on the base, through a parent trait of the component that declares them at the same JVM descriptor.
  - The third way would close `String`'s 7 and `Range`'s `isEmpty`.
  - It would not close `ReadableArray`'s `opr[_:TrivialOpenRange]`: the objects narrow its return type, which is the bridge case above.

- F-84 **In the interpreter's library, the result-only type parameters of `fail`, `builtinPrimitive` and `List`'s comprehension operator `BIG <|[\T\]|>` are unbounded, as the team declared them, and the same rung repaired 25 of the compiled checker's 60 one-off error sites in numbers, orderings, `List` and natives, each by a declared type, a body or an api header, in forms that the library already uses.** A result-only parameter occurs only in the result type. P-48 gives it the intersection of its upper bounds, narrowed by the expected type, so where `()` is expected its instance is `()`. The rung also made `MatchFailure` an unchecked exception: it extends `UncheckedException` (row 590). The sites that it left have rows (report section 5). Limit: under walk the name `IntLiteral` also denotes a value, a zero that no numeral reaches, and its arithmetic answers a `ZZ32` against its declared `IntLiteral` (row 578). F-263 holds the integer powers' types, and F-255 `List`'s ordering. Gated under walk by `tests/NumberOrderListDeclarations.fss`. Detail: `compile-ladder/rung-number-order-slips/REPORT.md` sections 1, 4 and 5.
Specification/basic/expressions/case.tex:60:If no matched clause is found, a \TYP{MatchFailure} exception is thrown.
Specification/basic/expressions/typecase.tex:99:If no matched clause is found, a \TYP{MatchFailure} exception is thrown
Specification/basic/expressions/typecase.tex:100:(\TYP{MatchFailure} is an unchecked exception).
